definitions.explanation: A green organelle found in plant cells and algae that carries out photosynthesis. Contains chlorophyll, which captures light energy and uses it to produce sugars from carbon dioxide and water.

examples.japanese: {葉|は}の{細胞|さいぼう}には{葉緑体|ようりょくたい}がある。
{葉緑体|ようりょくたい}で{光合成|こうごうせい}が{行|おこな}われる。
examples.english: Photosynthesis takes place in the chloroplasts.

examples.japanese: {葉緑体|ようりょくたい}には{葉緑素|ようりょくそ}という{緑色|みどりいろ}の{色素|しきそ}が{含|ふく}まれている。
examples.english: Chloroplasts contain a green pigment called chlorophyll.

examples.japanese: {葉緑体|ようりょくたい}は{独自|どくじ}のDNAを{持|も}ち、{細菌|さいきん}に{由来|ゆらい}すると{考|かんが}えられている。
examples.english: Chloroplasts have their own DNA and are thought to have originated from bacteria.

notes:
Composed of {葉緑|ようりょく} (leaf green, i.e., chlorophyll) and {体|たい} (body). A standard term from biology, learned in middle school and high school science.

USAGE:
- A plain technical noun; does not take する.
- Typically appears in biology textbooks and discussions of photosynthesis, cell structure, or plant evolution.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {葉緑体|ようりょくたい}を{持|も}つ: to have chloroplasts
- {葉緑体|ようりょくたい}で{光合成|こうごうせい}を{行|おこな}う: to perform photosynthesis in the chloroplasts
- {葉緑体|ようりょくたい}の{構造|こうぞう}: the structure of chloroplasts

RELATED WORDS:
- {葉緑素|ようりょくそ}: chlorophyll — the green pigment inside the chloroplast
- {光合成|こうごうせい}: photosynthesis — the process carried out in the chloroplast
- {細胞|さいぼう}: cell — chloroplasts are organelles inside plant cells
- ミトコンドリア: mitochondrion — another major organelle, responsible for energy production
